contracts.commit_point: asyncio.create_subprocess_exec in _run_once (middleware.py:145-150), reached via _exec from the read_resource branches (middleware.py:567, 576).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Per-task rate limit checked before any branch (middleware.py:555-557); the ConfigMap branch validates name and namespace against _NAME_PAT and returns BLOCKED on failure (559-564); the URL branch validates against _URL_PAT and returns BLOCKED on failure (571-573); both branches call _exec with literal argv lists (567, 576), and _run_once uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec — no shell — for argv lists (144-150).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Spawning a subprocess for an agent-supplied reference that fails validation — an invalid ConfigMap reference (name or namespace not matching _NAME_PAT) or a malformed URL (not matching _URL_PAT) returns BLOCKED — or reaching the spawn through any shell-interpolated string; only the fixed argv-list calls at middleware.py:567 and 576 are permitted commit forms.

contracts.protected_operation: The read_resource ConfigMap fetch and URL fetch, each executed via _exec on behalf of an agent-supplied path_or_url argument.
contracts.protected_resource: The executor host's subprocess surface (the kubectl/curl argv) reached from agent-supplied references, and the cluster API or network endpoints those binaries contact.
contracts.protection_obligation: ConfigMap and URL fetches requested through the read_resource tool must have the agent-supplied reference validated (DNS-label pattern for configmap name and namespace; strict http(s) URL pattern) and be executed only in the fixed argv forms (kubectl get configmap <name> -n <ns> -o yaml; curl -sL --max-time 15 -- <url>) before any subprocess spawn.
scope_limits: These branches do not pass through _pre_flight, assess_command, the autonomy engine, or the approval gate; the reviewers' assertion that read_resource operations pass the parser-based safety assessment is not supported by the supplied source.
Validation is format-only; the content of fetched ConfigMaps or URLs is returned to the agent unfiltered, and no content-level guard is declared here.
The read-only shape comes from the fixed argv (kubectl get / curl -sL); no independent mechanism beyond the fixed argv prevents other kubectl verbs through this path.

contracts.commit_point: p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')[:MAX_OUTPUT] at middleware.py:592 — the point where file contents are obtained for return to the agent.
contracts.declared_mechanism: read_resource resolves the requested path with pathlib.Path.resolve and checks p.is_relative_to(root) against get_settings().safety.read_paths before p.read_text (middleware.py:580-594); the per-task ToolRateLimiter is checked first (555-557); read_paths defaults to ['/etc/kopilot'] and an empty list disables file reads entirely (config.py:109-111).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Returning file contents to the agent for a requested path whose resolved location is not relative to any configured read_paths root (such requests are refused with 'BLOCKED: file reads are restricted to ...'); when read_paths is empty, all local file reads are disabled.

contracts.protected_operation: The read_resource local-file branch: reading a documentation file from the executor filesystem (pathlib read_text) and returning its contents to the agent.
contracts.protected_resource: The executor filesystem outside the configured read_paths roots; the readable set is confined to those roots (default ['/etc/kopilot'], config.py:109-111).
contracts.protection_obligation: Local-file reads served to the agent through the read_resource tool must resolve inside one of the configured safety.read_paths roots before the file's contents are read and returned to the agent.
scope_limits: Read-side (information-disclosure) restriction only; no filesystem mutation is guarded by this contract.
Covers only the local-file branch; the ConfigMap and URL branches of read_resource use different validation and commit paths.
The allowed-root set is deployment configuration (SAFETY_READ_PATHS); source fixes only the default value.
Check and read occur sequentially in one coroutine after resolve(); no claim is made about concurrent filesystem changes between the containment check and read_text.

contracts.commit_point: asyncio.create_subprocess_shell / asyncio.create_subprocess_exec inside _run_once (middleware.py:137-150), reached from _guarded_run via _run_and_record and _exec (middleware.py:287, 176-190).
contracts.declared_mechanism: _guarded_run (middleware.py:315-404) routes every command through _pre_flight (middleware.py:224-240: _BLOCKED_PATTERNS denylist at 226-228, ToolRateLimiter.check at 230-236, assess_command at 238) and the autonomy decision at 321, then refuses in observe mode (322-328), auto-approves under a recorded policy (329-352), consumes or creates a human approval request (354-385), or returns BLOCKED without executing (387-401); only a permitted verdict reaches _run_and_record and then _exec (345, 363, 404). assess_command (safety.py:427-485) blocks protected-namespace mutations outright (439-447), requires approval for all-namespace destructive operations (449-455), opaque commands (457-467), destructive verbs (469-475), and other mutations (477-483), with require_approval_destructive defaulting to true and protected_namespaces defaulting to the three system namespaces (config.py:96-112).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A tool-supplied command reaching the subprocess spawn without a permitting verdict, specifically: (a) any match against the _BLOCKED_PATTERNS catastrophic denylist (rm -rf /, --no-preserve-root, fork bomb, mkfs, dd of=/dev/, shutdown/reboot/halt, chmod 000 /, chown /, find / -delete, > /dev/[sh]d*); (b) any mutating command targeting a protected namespace (kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease) — allowed=False at CRITICAL risk with no approval path; (c) destructive operations across all namespaces — approval required; (d) opaque commands (unparseable pipelines, kubectl exec/cp/attach payloads, unrecognised binaries) — allowed only if require_approval_destructive is false, otherwise approval required; (e) destructive commands — approval required while require_approval_destructive is true (the default); (f) mutating commands not provably read-only — approval required; (g) any mutating command refused by autonomy level 0 or an engaged emergency brake.

contracts.protected_operation: Agent-invoked execution of kubectl, helm, and shell command strings via the run_kubectl/run_helm/run_shell tools collected in EXECUTOR_TOOLS.
contracts.protected_resource: The executor host's OS process/shell surface, and the Kubernetes cluster state reachable through kubectl/helm invoked on it, in particular the protected namespaces kube-system, kube-public, and kube-node-lease.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every kubectl, helm, or shell command string dispatched through the agent tools run_kubectl, run_helm, or run_shell must be blocked, refused, or held for explicit human approval — or affirmatively allowed — by the _guarded_run pipeline (_BLOCKED_PATTERNS denylist, per-task rate limiter, assess_command verdict, autonomy-engine decision, approval gate) before any subprocess is spawned for it; mutations of protected namespaces are blocked outright, and destructive/mutating/opaque commands are refused in observe mode or held for human approval.
scope_limits: Covers only run_kubectl, run_helm, and run_shell; read_resource does not pass through _guarded_run/_pre_flight/assess_command.

The gate is parser-based and fails toward approval, not outright blockage: commands _split_pipeline cannot parse are opaque and approval-gated unless they also hit the denylist or a protected namespace; the source itself states this gate is one layer behind scoped RBAC (safety.py:16-17, middleware.py:44-47).

Setting SAFETY_REQUIRE_APPROVAL_DESTRUCTIVE=false makes destructive/mutating/opaque verdicts allowed=True so those commands execute without approval (safety.py:459, 471, 479); this contract presumes the default true (config.py:102).
Autonomy-level auto-approval executes mutations without a human in the loop; its conditions live in kopilot.executor.autonomy, which is not among the supplied views.
Approval-gated commands can later execute via execute_approved; the execution-time re-check on that path is captured in a separate contract.
